input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper has the same shared-dict pattern: it clears the dict and binds the copy's and the outer local's statistics to it, so concurrent or nested invocations of the same decorated coroutine share and clobber one statistics dict.
- rationale: Trigger: two overlapping awaits of the same @retry-decorated coroutine, or a recursive await of it. Each invocation calls stats.clear() on the shared dict and then writes attempt_number and timing fields into it. Impact: each caller reads statistics that belong to another in-flight call, and the values are wrong or reset mid-call. The old code rebinding a fresh copy.statistics per call avoided this.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. One statistics dict is cleared and reused on every call, so concurrent or overlapping awaits of the decorated coroutine wipe each other's attempt_number and timing fields and read wrong stats. It covers the async-wrapper case that the label explicitly includes.
